documents.unit: Office of the Vice Provost for Education (AI Council)
documents.title: Tufts Generative AI Usage Guidelines for Faculty, Staff, and Students
documents.stance_why: The guidelines call themselves "deliberately non-prescriptive" and say "Faculty have the freedom and responsibility to determine appropriate AI use within their courses", noting faculty "may require AI use, permit it with conditions, discourage it, or prohibit it." They set no default rule, so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: Tufts' university-wide guidelines, adopted by the AI Council in spring 2026, set six principles (accountability, ethical responsibility, community trust, transparency, clarifying AI use, course expectations). They are deliberately non-prescriptive: instructors decide what AI use is allowed and should communicate it, and everyone should disclose substantive use and protect restricted data.

units.why: The course statement says there is 'no institution-wide policy' so each class decides; it is a statement that rules are set course by course (P04). It dates from before the 2026 guidelines.
units.anchor: Tufts University does not have an institution-wide policy on AI use in classes, on assignments,
units.fit_note: Describes absence of a university rule, an older statement. States that Tufts has no institution-wide policy and each class sets its own; this predates the Spring 2026 guidelines.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'Tufts University does not have an institution-wide policy on AI use in classes' with 'each class will have its own policies' is a statement of who sets the rule (P04); kept as a real statement, although it predates the 2026 guidelines (fit_note).

units.why: Defines GAI by listing tools and types of generated output; a definition that sets scope (P61).
units.anchor: “Generative Artificial Intelligence” (GAI) includes, but not limited to: Bing Chat Enterprise, ChatGPT, Google Bard,
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. The definition 'Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) includes, but not limited to: Bing Chat Enterprise, ChatGPT...' sets the scope of the course rule (P61), so kept.

units.why: Notes GAI's potential to benefit learning and compares it to collaboration with peers (brainstorming, feedback); a benefit statement, P87, with the peer comparison a secondary P45 point.
units.anchor: While there is potential for GAI to benefit learning, just as you would in collaboration
units.fit_note: Also compares AI to peer collaboration (P45).
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'While there is potential for GAI to benefit learning' states a benefit of AI within the course statement (P87), so kept.

units.why: Requires submitted work to 'reflect your own understanding and effort': ownership (P29). Reconciled codes: actor student, phase during-work, modality must, type P29, unit stance neutral.
units.anchor: all submitted work must reflect your own understanding and effort.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'all submitted work must reflect your own understanding and effort' is an authorship rule within the directing example (P29), so kept; unit stance neutral because it governs authorship, not whether AI may be used.

units.why: Warns AI gives 'confident but inaccurate information' and bias: P31.
units.anchor: AI can produce confident but inaccurate information (including invented references) and may reproduce bias.
units.resolution_why: Only B coded this. 'AI can produce confident but inaccurate information (including invented references) and may reproduce bias' is a warning that students must verify (P31), so kept as information.

notes: The CELT page embeds example policies from individual Tufts courses and hypothetical templates; their units are coded under the page's university layer, and unit_stance reflects each example's own position. The Intro to Computation for Engineers example says Tufts has no institution-wide AI policy, which predates the Spring 2026 guidelines. A few sentences are coded as more than one unit when they hold distinct rules. Reconciliation: Coder B. Two included documents. Doc 2 mixes CELT guidance with sample course statements (including one from an intro computation for engineers course saying Tufts has no institution-wide policy, which predates the 2026 guidelines); example statements are coded as units addressed to students.
